About me

AI & Machine Learning Engineer

I’m an AI and Machine Learning Engineer in Jönköping, Sweden, with an M.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence from Jönköping University. My hands-on experience runs across computer vision, image retrieval, NLP and optimisation, most of it built on industry-collaborative projects.

I’m currently an Artificial Intelligence Intern at Elajo Elektriska AB, taking an AI-assisted warranty claim system towards production. Python is my main language, C# my working second, and what interests me most is turning experimental models into software people can actually use.

Elajo Elektriska ABMaster’s thesis followed by internship2026

AI-assisted product identification for industrial warranty claims

Identifying electrical products from imperfect field photographs, then connecting the result to the warranty workflow.

5 vision modelsbenchmarked under one evaluation setup
Zero-shotno fine-tuning on in-house images
PyTorchDINOv2CLIPFAISSFastAPIReactASP.NETC#SQL ServerAzureGitHub Actions

Problem

Warranty photos are often blurred, partly occluded or missing a readable barcode. The catalogue, however, contains clean studio images.

Engineering approach

I benchmarked five pretrained vision models under a single evaluation setup, using Albumentations to simulate field degradation so the scores reflected the photographs the system would actually receive.

From prototype to integration

The thesis prototype combined React, FastAPI and SQL Server with automated eligibility checks and document generation. During the internship, the work expanded toward production with ASP.NET/C#, Azure AD authentication, ERP API integration, testing and CI/CD through GitHub Actions.

Master’s thesis published in DiVA ↗Paper in preparation for Computers in Industry (Elsevier)

Ongoing deployment work is governed by NDA.

Jönköping UniversityMaterials & Manufacturing2025

Turning research papers into structured materials data

A Dockerized document-processing application that turns aerospace research PDFs into structured, searchable datasets.

PythonPDFPlumberCamelotNLPPandasStreamlitDockerGemini API

Problem

Alloy compositions and material properties sit scattered across paragraphs and tables in scientific PDFs. Reading them out by hand does not scale.

What I built

A pipeline that cleans and segments PDF text, pulls tables with PDFPlumber and Camelot, then merges features from both into one dataset. Exported as CSV and Excel, searchable through Streamlit.

Engineering decision

Two parallel extraction routes rather than one. Text alone misses the tables, tables alone lose their context, so the merge is where the dataset comes from.

Selected work

Industry collaboration projects

Trackmate2025

EUR Pallet Image Classification

Can pretrained CNNs separate standardised EUR pallets from non-EUR ones, given only a small image dataset?

Problem

EUR pallets follow standardised dimensions, so automatic recognition would support sorting, inspection and logistics handling. The dataset available was 200 images, split 160 for training and 40 for validation.

Approach

Transfer learning with three ImageNet backbones, each given a new binary head, plus a fine-tuning stage for MobileNetV2 with layers unfrozen at a lower learning rate. Class weights handled the imbalance and augmentation covered variation the training images did not.

What I found

ResNet50 recorded the highest validation accuracy at 75%. With roughly 40 validation images and preprocessing that was not identical across every run, I treat these as indicative rather than conclusive.

Husgruppen2025

House Cost Prediction

Predicting Swedish villa construction costs from 22 real project records, published with Husgruppen’s permission.

Problem

Cost depends on house dimensions, structural components, delivery location, freight and snow zone. Twenty-two completed builds is very little to model from, so the work was as much about evaluation design as about prediction.

Approach

Engineered ratio features such as wall-to-roof and window-to-wall, selected the top ten by Random Forest importance, then compared Decision Tree, Random Forest and XGBoost tuned with GridSearchCV under five-fold cross-validation. Noise of ±2% expanded the 22 records to 242.

What I found

The tuned Decision Tree gave the lowest cross-validation error, around 12,200 SEK MAE. The more useful finding was a flaw in my own setup: the augmentation ran before the train/test split, so near-copies of the same villa sit on both sides and the reported error is optimistic. Grouping the original villas before augmenting is the fix.
